newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CS July 1 sugar stocks well below last year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CS July 1 sugar stocks well below last year.

text.p: Sugar stocks by July 1 in Brazil's center-south region are around 16.71 percent below the same stage last year, said independent consultants DataNet Agricommodities.
This was due to slightly lower sugar output compared with 1996/97 and because more sugar is being sold on the external market, DataNet said in a regular report.
By the end of the previous fortnightly period to June 16, DataNet had said that stocks were 7.66 percent down on 1996/97 levels.
Sugar production to July 1 reached 2.46 million tonnes, 1.82 percent below the 2.51 million tonnes seen at the same stage last year.

Sales to the internal market rose 5.43 percent or an additional 64,000 tonnes in the fortnight to July 1 compared with last year while sales on the international market were 31.37 percent higher or 189,000 tonnes.
The weather will be key over the coming fortnightly periods for the crop, DataNet said.

The critical moment will be between the second fortnight in August and the first week in September as historically the sugar content reaches its peak during this period and also then it should be possible to see the climatic impact of the El Nino phenomenon.
The phenomenon which is developing in the Pacific Ocean has resulted in an unusually warm month of July for Brazil's southeast region which includes the center-south.
The warm weather has led to a slight increase in consumption which together with higher sales to the overseas market has benefited domestic prices recently, DataNet said.
Average prices for crystal sugar in Sao Paulo state (without taxes) reached $10.77 a 50-kg bag in the third week of July, 18.66 percent below the equivalent price last year.
However in the first two weeks in July, prices were over 20 percent lower than at the same stage in 1996, DataNet said.
